transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-09
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~52m
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Alvaro Mendes (Prod), Evelyn Park (BlueHarbor CTO), Marco Ruiz (ML Eng), Sasha Kim (Product), Tom B. (SRE)

Summary: Short demo + sandboxed run showing low-latency fastpaths for chat, parameter walk-through, and live retry scenarios.

[00:00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll keep this hands-on, I'm Jordan lee, AE at Redwood. Priya will drive the console and run a small bench.
[00:00:12] Evelyn Park: Hi Jordan, thanks; Marco and I are mainly focused on 95pctl latency — our user chats need to feel instant.
[00:00:20] Priya Nair: Great — quick FYI we'll demonstrate a "fastpaths" runtime mode, that's our lower-latency exec path that avoids certain batching/kernel transitions for short sequences. It's not free — there's cost/throughput tradeoffs.
[00:00:35] Marco Ruiz: Sounds good — what's the latency delta and how brittle is it under tail load?
[00:00:42] Priya Nair: In our perf profiles, for short-turn dialogs (<= 128 tokens) fastpaths can cut 95pctl by 30-60% vs balanced kernels; under heavy burst it favours latency but may reduce overall throughput. We'll show console toggles.
[00:01:05] Tom B.: Quick question about data retention and logs — we'll need audit trails for compliance, SOC2 — do you have those in the hosted plan?
[00:01:12] Jordan Lee: Yes, hosted includes audit logs and redaction options; for stricter controls we recommend Dedicated or Private. We'll send SOC2 certs after.
[00:01:22] Priya Nair: Ok demo: I'm in the Redwood Console -> Sandbox project -> Model route. I'll enable fastpaths for the route and set params: max_tokens 128, temperature 0.2, top_p 0.95, response_chunk_size 64 bytes to encourage earlier streaming.
[00:01:45] [00:01:45] Priya Nair (screen): (narration) toggled fastpaths = ON, traffic % = 100% for this sandbox, batching policy set to single-request-prefer, prefix_cache = enabled for repeated system prompts.
[00:02:10] Sasha Kim: prefix_cache? can you explain that quickly?
[00:02:16] Priya Nair: Sure — prefix caching caches KV cache for unloaded repeated prefixes so subsequent requests avoid re-computing early layers. Good for assistants with stable system/preamble. It helps latency and cost.
[00:02:38] Marco Ruiz: Any gotchas with caching and safety/PII?
[00:02:42] Priya Nair: Caching respects customer isolation and TTL; you can disable or encrypt cache contents in Private. We'll send docs.
[00:02:55] [00:02:55] Jordan Lee: Let's trigger a live prompt — Marco, you sent a sample prompt earlier?
[00:03:02] Marco Ruiz: Yes — "Summarize the last 3 user messages and propose next actions" — it's typical for our flow.
[00:03:08] [00:03:08] Priya Nair: Sending request now with streaming enabled; note the console shows chunks as they arrive.
[00:03:23] [00:03:23] Speaker 1: (stream) "Sure, here's a brief summary..." — you can see the first chunk came in at ~60ms after tokenization finished on the node.
[00:03:35] Marco Ruiz: Nice. So streaming chunk size of 64 — is that bytes or tokens?
[00:03:41] Priya Nair: We expose response_chunk_size in bytes; we also have max_stream_delay which controls flush intervals to avoid tiny chattiness. For very low-latency UX we recommend 32–128 bytes and low delay.
[00:03:57] Evelyn Park: If a chunk fails mid-stream, what's the retry story?
[00:04:03] Priya Nair: Good question. On transient node failures we have two strategies: optimistic fast retry (repeat last request with idempotency token) and stream-resume where the client resumes from last acked token. The hosted API supports resumable streams for supported SDKs; otherwise we recommend idempotency_id per user-turn so retries are safe.
[00:04:28] Tom B.: That resume capability — does it require application-level state?
[00:04:32] Priya Nair: Minimal: the client records last-seen server offset and passes resume_id. The server stores short-lived offsets for active sessions. We'll include the resume API doc link.
[00:04:45] [00:04:45] Jordan Lee: Let's simulate a transient error — Priya, can you kill the instance in the sandbox to force a retry path?
[00:04:52] Priya Nair: Doing it now — note: we'll degrade gracefully to standard kernel; since fastpaths was on, the platform attempted a local retry and then failed over to balanced kernel.
[00:05:10] [00:05:10] Speaker 2: (noise) okay we saw a reconnect, client got a final 'partial' then a resumed stream entry. The SDK attempted two retries with exponential backoff (200ms, 400ms).
[00:05:25] Marco Ruiz: How many retries are safe before we risk duplicate side effects?
[00:05:30] Priya Nair: Use idempotency token per user-turn — server will dedupe replayed requests within a short window. For side effects, prefer function-calls with explicit ack.
[00:05:41] Evelyn Park: About billing — do fastpaths charge a premium?
[00:05:46] Jordan Lee: Yes we surface a fastpaths multiplier; it's typically 1.2–1.5x per-token compute because it biases low-latency kernels. We'll include estimated cost comparisons for your sample traffic.
[00:05:59] Sasha Kim: Can we run a short bench against our sample dataset?
[00:06:03] Jordan Lee: Absolutely — next steps: we'll provision trial keys and a sandbox route. Priya will run a 10k-turn bench with your prompts and share the 50/95/99pctl.
[00:06:13] [00:06:13] Priya Nair: Now switching to Optimize tab — this routes suggested param changes based on measured latency/cost. See recommended: lower response_chunk_size to 48 and enable aggressive prefix_cache for this workload. It predicts 95pctl drop ~28% and +8% cost.
[00:06:33] Marco Ruiz: Is there automated rollbacks if latency spikes?
[00:06:36] Priya Nair: Yes console can set a rollback policy: if 95pctl > threshold or error rate increases, we can auto-fallback from fastpaths to balanced or to a cheaper model variant.
[00:06:48] Tom B.: For security reviews — we need SAML SSO and logs shipped to our SIEM, plus KMS integration.
[00:06:54] Jordan Lee: SAML and KMS supported for Dedicated and Private; for hosted we offer SSO and log export; we'll attach our compliance matrix.
[00:07:06] [00:07:06] Evelyn Park: Any recommendations on batching? We worry about throughput at peak — we don't want fastpaths to blow up cloud spend.
[00:07:12] Priya Nair: Batching is great for throughput — if you have many parallel users with long sessions, set batching policy to auto and use fastpaths for low concurrency user-facing flows. We often recommend hybrid: fastpaths for interactive, batch for background summarization.
[00:07:32] Marco Ruiz: Are there limits on concurrent fastpaths routes per account?
[00:07:36] Jordan Lee: In hosted it's soft-limited and we can raise quotas; Dedicated gives guaranteed capacity.
[00:07:45] [00:07:45] Priya Nair: Ok switching back to the live SDK — I'll show the idempotency header and resume API call in code. (reads) Example: POST /v1/chat with idempotency_key: user-turn-123, stream: true. On retry, include resume_token to pull the rest.
[00:08:10] Marco Ruiz: The SDK auto-manages idempotency?
[00:08:13] Priya Nair: Our JS and Python SDKs expose a convenience wrapper that generates and stores idempotency keys per turn; they also implement resumable stream handlers.
[00:08:25] Sasha Kim: A weird edge: if we have function-calls in the middle, do they get executed twice on retry?
[00:08:31] Priya Nair: Function-calls can be marked transactional; the runtime will only surface the function call to your webhook once if idempotency is present — otherwise app should dedupe.
[00:08:44] [00:08:44] Jordan Lee: Let's do a short Q&A — any blockers for starting a pilot?
[00:08:50] Evelyn Park: We need bench results, cost estimate, and SOC2 docs. Also timeline: can we run pilot next week?
[00:08:58] Jordan Lee: Yes — we'll aim to kick off bench next week.
[00:09:04] Tom B.: Can we get a config that auto-scales between fastpaths and balanced by hour-of-day?
[00:09:09] Priya Nair: You can do time-based routing in the console and set different policies by policy group — we'll include a sample policy JSON.
[00:09:20] Marco Ruiz: One last thing — do you support quantized model variants for faster inference on fastpaths?
[00:09:25] Priya Nair: Yes we have quantized variants; fastpaths can select quantized kernels when supported, though some model behaviors differ slightly — Optimize recommends by workload.
[00:09:40] [00:09:40] Alvaro Mendes: We'll attach the fastpaths-playbook which covers tuning, cost math and guardrails.
[00:09:46] Evelyn Park: Great, thanks.
[00:09:49] [00:09:49] Jordan Lee: Recap and next steps: Jordan to share pricing + SOC2, Priya to run bench and upload results, Marco to share prompts and latency targets. We'll schedule 30m bench review next Wed.
[00:10:05] (meeting continues with small side discussions and clarifications; demo session consumed ~18 minutes, bench planning and security discussion took ~34 minutes; end)

Questions captured:
- Can fastpaths be auto-rolled back on tail latency spikes? (Yes; config shown)
- How to avoid duplicate side-effects on retries? (Idempotency tokens + transactional function calls)
- What's the billing uplift for fastpaths? (Approx 1.2–1.5x)
